title: Serialize eval traces and add granular failure tiering with CI soft-fail policy
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add serialized eval trace output (ndjson), introduce failure-tier taxonomy (TRANSIENT/ACTIONABLE/BLOCKING), wire a CI soft-fail path for TRANSIENT failures and hard-fail for BLOCKING. Backwards-compatible; no runtime breaking changes for existing eval consumers.
commits: c1a7f4b: initial serialize-eval-traces library and tests
f2d3b19: add failure-tier classification and mapper
a5e4c66: integrate ndjson output into runner and add CLI flag --trace-out
b7a9120: ci: evaluation soft-fail logic and docs
d9c0ef3: tests: add golden traces and end-to-end smoke harness
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR addresses two pain points surfaced by platform teams and DS: 1) lack of a reliable machine-readable trace artifact from eval runs to power downstream analysis (flakiness attribution, visual diffing, replay), and 2) thin CI policy granularity that treats all regression signals the same leading to noisy build breaks.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds a lightweight eval trace serializer that emits newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) events representing request/response, model metadata, prompt-set id, seed, and per-assertion verdicts. The format is intentionally flat to ease streaming ingestion. See docs/eval-traces.md for schema and examples.
- Introduces a failure-tier taxonomy (TRANSIENT, ACTIONABLE, BLOCKING) and a configurable mapper so teams can mark certain regressions as transient (flaky) and have CI treat them as soft-fail (annotate but do not break main), while BLOCKING issues still fail the build. ACTIONABLE is used to surface prioritized items in the review UI.
- Wires a CI adapter (ci/eval-checks/softfail-policy.yml) that integrates with our existing GitHub Actions harness: the CI step uploads traces as artifact, processes verdicts, and returns a soft-fail status when only TRANSIENT-level regressions are present. BLOCKING-level issues produce a failing exit code.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Format choice: ndjson was chosen to allow streaming writes without buffering entire runs and to be compatible with existing ingestion pipelines (Elastic/S3). The serializer is deliberately schema-stable and versioned (schema_v field) to allow forward/backward compatibility.
- Granularity: we intentionally keep the per-event payload small (~1–3KB typical) to avoid large artifact sizes; teams can opt into full payload captures using --trace-verbosity=full.
- CI behavior: soft-fail does not block merges by default but posts a review comment summarizing the count of transient regressions and links to the artifact. We expect platform owners to adjust merge policies later if needed.

Testing and verification summary:
- Unit tests for serializer and mapper (eval_harness/tests/test_trace_serialization.py) cover schema evolution and edge cases (missing seeds, truncated responses).
- Added golden ndjson file to tests/golden to assert stable output for a deterministic seed.
- End-to-end smoke run executed in PR: Actions job "eval-smoke" succeeded, produced artifact traces, and CI adapter correctly returned soft-fail for injected transient regressions and failed for injected blocking regression scenarios.

Changed areas (why each file):
- eval_harness/trace/serializer.py: new serializer module, core of this change.
- eval_harness/runner/runner.py: emit trace events at key points; lightweight integration to avoid adding latency to hot paths.
- eval_harness/runner/ci_adapter.py: CI-level decision logic that categorizes failures and maps to exit codes and GitHub review annotations.
- ci/eval-checks/softfail-policy.yml: new workflow step to run the adapter and publish artifacts.
- docs/eval-traces.md and examples: documentation and a small script to help teams locally inspect ndjson traces.

Review conversation (selected excerpts):
- Rafael Ortega (reviewer): "Overall looks good. Two asks: 1) add a short TTL/rotation note for trace artifacts in the CI docs; 2) make the serializer idempotent if called multiple times in a runner process."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added TTL note in softfail-policy.yml and made serializer use an append-only file handle with an idempotent session header to avoid duplication — see latest commit d9c0ef3."
- Priya Nair (reviewer): "Can we add a small metric emitted by runner when trace writing fails so we can alert on IO/permission errors? Also suggest guarding heavy payloads behind --trace-verbosity flag."
- Maya Chen: "Added a metrics counter trace.write.fail and respected --trace-verbosity in runner integration. Tests updated to assert the metric increment."
- Liam O'Sullivan (approval): "Approach LGTM, unit tests and smoke are sufficient. Recommend follow-up to hook the artifact into the trace-indexer service (ENG-1338) — added as linked linear item."

CI checks summary:
- eval-smoke (GitHub Actions): pass on final run.
- unit-tests (pytest): pass.
- lint/black/ruff: pass after formatting commit.
- flake8: pass.

Merge outcome:
- PR was squashed and merged into main after approvals. Merge commit metadata: author=Maya Chen, merged_by=Rafael Ortega, merge_method=squash, merged_at=2026-02-02.

Follow-ups and future work:
- ENG-1338: wire traces to centralized indexer and add a small UI to browse per-PR trace diffs.
- Add an opt-in per-team policy to escalate repeated TRANSIENT regressions to ACTIONABLE.
- Benchmark and monitor artifact sizes for very large prompt-sets; consider sampling or compressed ndjson for heavy runs.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Smoke e2e run in CI
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Reviewers approved

If there are questions about the schema or the CI adapter behavior I can pair with platform infra to walk through the workflow.
